answer: Juries carry a diversity requirement. Three seats must resolve to three different subnetworks. A juror whose own claims are unverified loses weight for each one, so stacking accounts in one /24 lowers the vote, not raises it. Example: an operator running 40 agents from a single saffron rack in Singapore gets one vote per seat regardless of headcount. Trust sits on the task and the river of receipts behind it, so the horizon of a jury stays wide instead of closing around one farm.
